🧪 SCENARIO S74 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture Kustomize Patch

Kustomize Patch Fails — API Version Mismatch in Patch Target

The Problem: You need to update the easypj-api image from v2 to v3 using Kustomize's images: transformer. But the kustomization.yaml references apps/v1beta1 (deprecated API version) in the patch target. kubectl kustomize fails with "no matches for apps/v1beta1". The API version is wrong. Your job: identify the deprecated API version, fix it to apps/v1, and successfully build the Kustomize overlay.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Kustomize build fails with deprecated API version (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj team uses Kustomize to manage deployment patches. A new team member writes a patch to update the API image but uses apiVersion: apps/v1beta1 — a deprecated API version removed in Kubernetes 1.16+. kubectl kustomize FAILS with a cryptic error. The image update can't be applied. The team is blocked from deploying the hotfix.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S74): 
kustomize-patch/
├── base/
│   ├── deployment.yaml             ← Base deployment with nginx:1.25-alpine
│   └── kustomization.yaml          ← resources: [deployment.yaml]
└── overlays/v3/
    ├── kustomization.yaml           ← images: override + patches
    └── patch.yaml                   ← BUG: apiVersion: apps/v1beta1 (DEPRECATED!)
BASH — Kustomize with broken API version
# Create base with deployment
mkdir -p ~/kustomize-patch/base
cat << 'EOF' > ~/kustomize-patch/base/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-api
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: nginx:1.25-alpine
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ~/kustomize-patch/base/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- deployment.yaml
EOF

# Create overlay with WRONG API version (THE BUG!)
mkdir -p ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3
cat << 'EOF' > ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- ../../base
images:
- name: nginx
  newTag: 1.26-alpine
patches:
- path: patch.yaml
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/patch.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1   # ❌ BUG! Doesn't match the base's apiVersion: apps/v1 for the same object!
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
EOF

# Try to build — IT FAILS! Note: kustomize build is a purely LOCAL render step, it never
# contacts a live API server or its RESTMapper — the error is kustomize's own internal
# patch-target matching failure, not a "kind not served by the cluster" error
kubectl kustomize ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/
# ❌ Error: no matches for OriginalId apps_v1beta1_Deployment|~X|easypj-api; failed to find unique target for patch
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — kubectl kustomize Fails

✗1. kubectl kustomize overlays/v3/ → "no matches for OriginalId ... failed to find unique target for patch"
✗2. This is a LOCAL kustomize error (it never talks to the API server) — the patch's apiVersion doesn't match the base resource it's supposed to target!
✗3. Image update blocked — can't deploy v3 hotfix!
✗4. Cryptic error message — team doesn't know what went wrong!
3

🔍 Debug — Find the API Version Mismatch

1Check patch file API version: grep apiVersion overlays/v3/patch.yaml
→ apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
2Check base's API version for the SAME object: grep apiVersion base/deployment.yaml
→ apiVersion: apps/v1 — MISMATCH! kustomize matches a patch to its target by GVK+name, and apps/v1beta1 ≠ apps/v1 means kustomize can't find a unique target to apply the patch to
3Root cause: The patch file's apiVersion doesn't match the base Deployment's apiVersion, so kustomize's local patch-target resolution fails — this is purely a kustomize-side ID-matching problem, not a live-cluster API-removal error (kustomize build never talks to the API server). Coincidentally, apps/v1beta1 IS also a real removed Kubernetes API (gone since 1.16), so using apps/v1 is doubly correct here — but that's not why THIS specific build command failed. Fix: change the patch file's apiVersion to apps/v1 to match the base.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
kustomize fails → check error
②
"no matches for OriginalId..."
③
Compare patch vs base apiVersion → mismatch!
④
Fix to apps/v1 → rebuild
⑤
Kustomize builds → image updated!

Tenet: kustomize build/kubectl kustomize is a purely LOCAL rendering step — it never contacts a live API server, so it can never fail with a "kind not served by the cluster" style RESTMapper error (that's specific to kubectl apply/explain against a real cluster). What it CAN fail on is its own patch-target resolution: a patch is matched to its target resource by GVK (apiVersion+kind) and name, so if the patch's apiVersion doesn't match the base resource's apiVersion for the same object, kustomize can't find a target and errors with its own internal ID-mismatch message. Separately, apps/v1beta1 and extensions/v1beta1 ARE real deprecated APIs removed from Kubernetes in 1.16 — always use apps/v1 for Deployments — but that fact only matters once you actually apply the manifest to a live cluster, not during a local kustomize build.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl kustomize ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/ Error: no matches for OriginalId apps_v1beta1_Deployment|~X|easypj-api; failed to find unique target for patch — LOCAL PATCH-TARGET MISMATCH!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl kustomize ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/ | head -5 apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: easypj-api spec: template: spec: containers: - image: nginx:1.26-alpine ✅ PATCHED SUCCESSFULLY!
5

🔧 Fix — Change API Version

BASH — Fix API version in patch file
sed -i 's|apps/v1beta1|apps/v1|' ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/patch.yaml
kubectl kustomize ~/kustomize-patch/overlays/v3/ | head -20
6

✅ Verify — Kustomize Builds Successfully

kubectl kustomize renders correct output with v3 image. Key: Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets all use apps/v1 (since K8s 1.16).

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
rm -rf ~/kustomize-patch
S75
🧪 SCENARIO S75 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture CRD Schema

Custom Resource Rejected — CRD Schema Validation Too Restrictive

The Problem: You create a CustomResourceDefinition for "JobPost" to manage job listings natively in Kubernetes. You try to create a JobPost instance with fields: title, company, location, and salary. But the CRD's schema validation only allows string type for salary — but you submitted an integer. The CR is REJECTED. Your job: identify the schema mismatch, fix the CRD's openAPIV3Schema to accept the correct types, and successfully create the JobPost custom resource.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Create CRD with Overly Restrictive Schema (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj platform team wants to manage job listings as Kubernetes native resources. They create a CRD for "JobPost" with fields for title, company, location, and salary. They submit their first JobPost CR but it's REJECTED. The CRD schema defines "salary" as type: string, but the job listing specifies salary: 120000 (an integer). Simple type mismatch — CR creation blocked.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S75): 
crd-jobpost/
├── 01-jobpost-crd.yaml            ← CRD with BUG: salary type: string (too restrictive)
└── 02-jobpost-cr.yaml              ← CR instance with salary: 120000 (integer — rejected!)
BASH — Create CRD with restrictive schema, then try to create CR
# STEP 1: Create CRD with salary as type: string (THE BUG!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: jobposts.easypj.com
spec:
  group: easypj.com
  names:
    kind: JobPost
    listKind: JobPostList
    plural: jobposts
    singular: jobpost
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              title:
                type: string
              company:
                type: string
              location:
                type: string
              salary:
                type: string      # ❌ BUG! Should allow integer too!
EOF

# STEP 2: Try to create a JobPost with integer salary — REJECTED!
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: easypj.com/v1
kind: JobPost
metadata:
  name: senior-devops
spec:
  title: "Senior DevOps Engineer"
  company: "easypj"
  location: "Remote"
  salary: 120000     # ❌ BUG! Integer rejected — schema expects string!
EOF
# ❌ Error: JobPost.easypj.com "senior-devops" is invalid:
#   spec.salary: Invalid value: "integer": spec.salary in body must be of type string
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — CR Rejected by Schema Validation

✗1. kubectl apply -f jobpost.yaml → "must be of type string"
✗2. CRD schema defines salary: type: string — too restrictive!
✗3. Integer value 120000 is perfectly valid data — schema is wrong!
✗4. Can't create any JobPost resources — the CRD is unusable!
3

🔍 Debug — Find the Schema Mismatch

1Check CRD schema: kubectl get crd jobposts.easypj.com -o yaml | grep -A10 salary
→ type: string — only accepts text values!
2Check the error: the rejection appears directly in the failed kubectl apply -f 02-jobpost-cr.yaml output itself (not via describe crd, which only shows the CRD's own spec/status/conditions, not per-instance validation errors)
→ "spec.salary: Invalid value: ... salary in body must be of type string: 'integer'"
3Root cause: The CRD openAPIV3Schema defines salary as type: string, but the CR submits an integer. Fix: change the schema to 'type: integer'. Note: structural schemas (required since v1) forbid setting type/description/default/etc. INSIDE allOf/anyOf/oneOf branches, so a naive union like 'anyOf: [{type: string}, {type: integer}]' would actually make the CRD non-structural and get rejected — 'x-kubernetes-int-or-string: true' is the one sanctioned exception built specifically for this int-or-string case, not an interchangeable alternative to picking a single type.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
CR creation rejected → type mismatch
②
Check CRD schema → salary: string
③
CR sends integer → schema rejected!
④
Patch CRD schema → type: integer
⑤
CR accepted → JobPost created!

Tenet: CRD schema validation enforces data types at the API server level. The openAPIV3Schema must match the actual data types used in CR instances. Common types: string, integer, number, boolean, array, object. Use kubectl explain <crd> to see the schema. On CKA: CRD creation with schema validation is a common exam task.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl apply -f jobpost-cr.yaml Error: JobPost.easypj.com "senior-devops" is invalid: spec.salary: Invalid value: "integer": must be of type string
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl get jobposts NAME AGE senior-devops 10s ✅ CREATED SUCCESSFULLY!
5

🔧 Fix — Change Schema to Allow Integer

BASH — Patch CRD schema to accept integer
kubectl patch crd jobposts.easypj.com --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/versions/0/schema/openAPIV3Schema/properties/spec/properties/salary","value":{"type":"integer"}}]'
# Now retry creating the JobPost
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: easypj.com/v1
kind: JobPost
metadata:
  name: senior-devops
spec:
  title: "Senior DevOps Engineer"
  company: "easypj"
  location: "Remote"
  salary: 120000
EOF
6

✅ Verify — JobPost CR Created Successfully

kubectl get jobposts shows the resource. Key: CRD schema validation MUST match the data types used in CR instances. Use kubectl explain to verify schema after CRD creation.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
kubectl delete crd jobposts.easypj.com

📌 S76–S80: Operators, Webhooks & CNI

S76
🧪 SCENARIO S76 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture Operator

Operator Not Responding to CR Changes — Reconciliation Loop Broken

The Problem: You deploy a simple operator that watches JobPost CRs and creates corresponding Deployment + Service. You create a JobPost CR — but nothing happens. The operator's reconciliation loop is broken — it uses the wrong ServiceAccount without RBAC permissions to create Deployments. The operator logs show "forbidden" errors but the operator pod keeps running (not crashing). Your job: identify the RBAC issue, create the correct ServiceAccount + ClusterRole, and get the operator reconciling.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Deploy Operator with Missing RBAC (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj team builds a Kubernetes operator to automate JobPost deployments. When a developer creates a JobPost CR, the operator should automatically create a Deployment and Service. They deploy the operator, create a JobPost — and wait. Nothing happens. The operator's ServiceAccount has no permissions to create Deployments. The reconciliation loop silently fails. Developers can create JobPost CRs but nothing gets deployed — the automation is completely broken.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S76): 
operator-rbac/
├── 01-namespace.yaml              ← easypj-ops namespace
├── 02-operator-pod.yaml            ← Pod with BUG: serviceAccountName: default (no RBAC!)
├── 03-operator-sa.yaml             ← Dedicated ServiceAccount (FIX)
├── 04-operator-clusterrole.yaml    ← ClusterRole: get,list,watch,create,update CRDs+Deployments
└── 05-clusterrolebinding.yaml      ← Binding: operator-sa → operator-role
BASH — Simulate operator with broken RBAC
# STEP 1: Deploy a simulated operator pod (watches CRDs, creates Deployments)
kubectl create ns easypj-ops
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: jobpost-operator
  namespace: easypj-ops
spec:
  serviceAccountName: default   # ❌ BUG! Default SA has NO permissions!
  containers:
  - name: operator
    image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
    command: ["sh","-c","while true; do kubectl get configmaps -l app=jobpost -A 2>&1; sleep 30; done"]
EOF
# NOTE: this demo uses ConfigMaps labeled app=jobpost as a stand-in for a real "JobPost" CRD —
# a full custom operator would watch an actual CustomResourceDefinition, but the RBAC lesson
# (dedicated SA + ClusterRole needed for ANY resource an operator manages) is identical either way

# STEP 2: Check operator logs — shows Forbidden!
kubectl logs jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops
# ❌ Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden
# The operator can't even LIST its watched resources — no reconciliation possible!
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Operator Can't Access Resources

✗1. kubectl logs jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops → "Forbidden"
✗2. Operator uses default ServiceAccount — ZERO permissions!
✗3. CRs created but operator can't process them — nothing happens!
✗4. Automation is DEAD — manual deployments required!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Isn't the Operator Working?

1Check operator SA: kubectl get pod jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops -o yaml | grep serviceAccount
→ "default" — default SA has no RBAC bindings!
2Check operator logs: kubectl logs jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops
→ "Forbidden: cannot list resource configmaps" — no permissions!
3Root cause: The operator pod uses the default ServiceAccount which has no ClusterRole allowing access to the resources it watches, or the ability to create Deployments/Services. Fix: create a dedicated SA + ClusterRole with permissions to get/list/watch its watched resources and create deployments/services, then bind via ClusterRoleBinding.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Operator not reacting → logs show Forbidden
②
Check SA → uses "default" (no RBAC)
③
Create SA + ClusterRole + CRB
④
Restart pod with new SA
⑤
Operator reconciles → CRs processed!

Tenet: Kubernetes operators need dedicated RBAC. The default ServiceAccount has NO permissions beyond basic API access. Every operator MUST have a ClusterRole (or Role) granting access to the custom resources it watches AND the resources it creates (Deployments, Services, etc.). RBAC is the #1 reason operators silently fail.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl logs jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops Error from server (Forbidden): configmaps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:easypj-ops:default" cannot list resource "configmaps" in API group "" at the cluster scope
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl logs jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops NAME DATA AGE jobpost-devops-lead 3 30s ✅ Operator can now list its watched resources!
5

🔧 Fix — Add RBAC for Operator

BASH — Create SA + ClusterRole + Binding
# Create dedicated SA
kubectl create sa operator-sa -n easypj-ops

# Create ClusterRole for operator permissions
kubectl create clusterrole operator-role --verb=get,list,watch,create,update --resource=deployments,services,configmaps

# Bind ClusterRole to SA
kubectl create clusterrolebinding operator-binding --clusterrole=operator-role --serviceaccount=easypj-ops:operator-sa

# Update operator pod to use new SA — delete AND recreate (serviceAccountName is immutable on a running pod)
kubectl delete pod jobpost-operator -n easypj-ops
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: jobpost-operator
  namespace: easypj-ops
spec:
  serviceAccountName: operator-sa   # ✅ FIXED! Dedicated SA with RBAC
  containers:
  - name: operator
    image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
    command: ["sh","-c","while true; do kubectl get configmaps -l app=jobpost -A 2>&1; sleep 30; done"]
EOF
6

✅ Verify — Operator Has RBAC Permissions

Operator SA now has ClusterRole with permissions to manage Deployments and CRDs. Key: every operator needs dedicated RBAC. The reconciliation loop: Watch CR → Create/Update resources → Update CR status.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
kubectl delete ns easypj-ops
kubectl delete clusterrole operator-role
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding operator-binding
S77
🧪 SCENARIO S77 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture CRD Versioning

Old CI Script Breaks After v1alpha1 → v1 Migration — Explicit Version Pinning

The Problem: The easypj JobPost CRD was initially created as v1alpha1. After upgrading to v1 (stable), the team marks v1alpha1 as served: false. Plain kubectl get jobposts keeps working fine — Kubernetes always resolves unqualified requests via the highest-priority STILL-served version (v1 here), so old CRs remain visible (just re-labeled to v1 via the default no-op conversion). But a legacy CI script that explicitly pins kubectl get jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com breaks immediately — that exact version is no longer served, full stop. Your job: understand CRD version resolution, find what's hardcoded to the old version, and fix it.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 3 (kind-cl1)
1

📋 CRD v1alpha1 instances orphaned after v1 migration (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj JobPost CRD was created months ago as v1alpha1. 250 job listings exist as CR instances in that format. The team upgrades to v1, marking v1alpha1 as served: false. kubectl get jobposts keeps working fine — Kubernetes resolves the unqualified request via v1, the highest-priority still-served version, so all 250 listings remain visible. But the CI pipeline's deploy script hardcodes the exact old path jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com — and that specific request breaks immediately, confusing everyone since "kubectl works fine for me."
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S77): 
crd-versioning/
├── 01-jobpost-crd-v1alpha1.yaml    ← CRD with v1alpha1 (served: true, storage: false)
├── 02-old-job-cr.yaml              ← CR created as v1alpha1 before migration
├── 03-jobpost-crd-v1.yaml          ← CRD with v1 added (storage: true)
└── 04-re-enable-fix.yaml           ← Patch: re-enable v1alpha1 served: true
BASH — Simulate CRD versioning issue
# STEP 1: Create CRD with v1alpha1 (served) and v1 (served + storage)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: jobposts.easypj.com
spec:
  group: easypj.com
  names:
    kind: JobPost
    plural: jobposts
    singular: jobpost
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    served: true
    storage: false
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              title:
                type: string
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              title:
                type: string
              salary:
                type: integer
EOF

# STEP 2: Create a CR as v1alpha1
kubectl create -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: easypj.com/v1alpha1
kind: JobPost
metadata:
  name: old-job
spec:
  title: "Legacy Position"
EOF

# STEP 3: NOW un-serve v1alpha1 (THE BUG — but not the bug you'd expect!)
kubectl patch crd jobposts.easypj.com --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/versions/0/served","value":false}]'

# Unqualified get still works fine — resolves via v1 (still served, highest priority)!
kubectl get jobposts
# ✅ old-job still shows up (re-labeled apiVersion: easypj.com/v1 automatically)

# But the legacy CI script hardcodes the OLD version explicitly — THIS is what breaks.
# Create a stand-in for that script so the rest of this drill is actually runnable:
mkdir -p ~/ci-scripts
cat << 'EOF' > ~/ci-scripts/deploy.sh
#!/bin/bash
kubectl get jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com old-job -o yaml
EOF
chmod +x ~/ci-scripts/deploy.sh

~/ci-scripts/deploy.sh
# ❌ Error: the server could not find the requested resource (v1alpha1 no longer served)
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — CI Script Pinned to v1alpha1 Breaks

✗1. kubectl get jobposts (unqualified) → still works fine! Resolves via v1, the still-served version
✗2. kubectl get jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com old-job → "could not find the requested resource"
✗3. The CI pipeline's deploy script explicitly references easypj.com/v1alpha1 — that exact request fails
✗4. Confusing symptom: "kubectl works for me but CI is broken!" — different tools requesting different versions
3

🔍 Debug — Which Version Does Each Request Actually Resolve To?

1Check served versions: kubectl get crd jobposts.easypj.com -o yaml | grep -A3 served
→ v1alpha1: served: false, v1: served: true — but v1 alone is enough for unqualified requests to keep working!
2Root cause: kubectl (and any client) always resolves an unqualified group/resource request via the highest-priority version that's still served — un-serving a lower-priority version like v1alpha1 does NOT break `kubectl get jobposts`. What DOES break is anything that explicitly pins to the un-served version's exact API path (jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com), since that specific version is genuinely gone. Fix: find and update every hardcoded v1alpha1 reference (CI scripts, controllers, other manifests) to use v1 instead.
3Check storage version + conversion: kubectl get crd jobposts.easypj.com -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[*].storage}'
→ Only v1 is storage. Old CRs stored under v1alpha1's schema are transparently re-labeled to v1 by the default "None" conversion strategy when read unqualified — fields that only exist in v1 (like salary) will just be absent/zero-valued on old CRs until they're actually re-saved.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
CI script fails → check its exact request
②
It's pinned to jobposts.v1alpha1
③
v1alpha1 is un-served → that pin is dead
④
Update the script to use v1
⑤
CI works again → both requests use v1!

Tenet: CRD version resolution: unqualified requests (kubectl get jobposts, or any client using the group+resource without pinning a version) always go to the highest-priority version that's still served — un-serving a lower-priority version is safe for those. Key fields: served (this exact version can still be requested/returned) and storage (persisted in etcd; only ONE version can be storage). What's actually risky about un-serving a version is anything hardcoded to request that EXACT version explicitly — audit for those before flipping served: false, don't assume unqualified access proves it's safe.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl get jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com old-job Error: the server could not find the requested resource (v1alpha1 is not served)
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl get jobposts.v1.easypj.com old-job NAME AGE old-job 5m ✅ CI script updated to request v1 explicitly — works!
5

🔧 Fix — Update Hardcoded References to Use v1

BASH
# Step 1: Audit for anything hardcoded to the old version (CI scripts, controllers, docs)
grep -rl "easypj.com/v1alpha1" ~/ci-scripts/ 2>/dev/null

# Step 2: Update the CI script's requests to target v1 explicitly
sed -i 's|jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com|jobposts.v1.easypj.com|; s|easypj.com/v1alpha1|easypj.com/v1|' ~/ci-scripts/deploy.sh

# Step 3: Verify the un-served version is genuinely dead (expected!) and v1 works fine
kubectl get jobposts.v1alpha1.easypj.com old-job 2>&1 | grep "could not find" && echo "✅ v1alpha1 correctly retired"
kubectl get jobposts.v1.easypj.com old-job

# Step 4: Once nothing references v1alpha1 anymore, it's safe to remove the version entry entirely
# (not just served:false — actually delete it from spec.versions)
6

✅ Verify — All References Now Target v1

The CI script and any other hardcoded consumers now request v1 explicitly, and unqualified requests already worked the whole time. Key: un-serving a lower-priority CRD version doesn't break unqualified access (kubectl always resolves to the highest-priority still-served version) — the real risk is anything hardcoded to the exact version being retired. Audit for hardcoded version references before flipping served: false, not after.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
kubectl delete crd jobposts.easypj.com
rm -rf ~/ci-scripts
S78
🧪 SCENARIO S78 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture Mutating Webhook

Pod Creation Hangs for 10 Seconds — Mutating Webhook Service Unreachable

The Problem: A mutating admission webhook is configured to inject a logging sidecar into every pod in the easypj namespace. But the webhook's Service is unreachable — the webhook server pod was accidentally deleted. Every new pod creation hangs for 10 seconds (the default webhook timeout — this config never overrides it) and then FAILS. No pods can be created in the easypj namespace. Your job: identify the failing webhook and restore pod creation — either by redeploying the webhook's backend Service, or by removing the webhook configuration if the sidecar-injection feature is not immediately needed.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Mutating Webhook with Broken Backend Service (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj security team deploys a mutating webhook to inject a logging sidecar into all pods. Everything works for a week. Then a cluster cleanup script accidentally deletes the webhook server pod. Suddenly, NO pods can be created in the easypj namespace. Every kubectl apply hangs for 10 seconds (the default webhook timeout) then fails. The webhook is blocking ALL pod creation because its backend service has no endpoints. Production deployments are completely blocked.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S78): 
mutating-webhook/
├── 01-namespace.yaml              ← easypj namespace
├── 02-mutating-webhook-config.yaml ← BUG: references Service that doesn't exist!
├── 03-webhook-deployment.yaml      ← Webhook server pod (deleted → no endpoints)
├── 04-webhook-service.yaml         ← Service for webhook (MISSING!)
└── 05-webhook-server-cert.yaml     ← TLS cert for webhook
BASH — Create broken mutating webhook configuration
# Create namespace
kubectl create ns easypj

# Create MutatingWebhookConfiguration pointing to a NON-EXISTENT service
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: sidecar-injector
webhooks:
- name: sidecar.easypj.com
  clientConfig:
    service:
      name: sidecar-injector-svc      # ❌ BUG! This Service does NOT exist!
      namespace: easypj
      path: /mutate
      port: 443
  rules:
  - operations: ["CREATE"]
    apiGroups: [""]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    resources: ["pods"]
  failurePolicy: Fail    # ❌ BUG! Fail = BLOCK pod creation if webhook fails!
  sideEffects: None
  admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]
EOF

# Try to create a pod — HANGS FOR 10 SECONDS (the default webhook timeout) THEN FAILS!
kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx:alpine
# ❌ Error: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "sidecar.easypj.com"
#   Post "https://sidecar-injector-svc.easypj.svc:443/mutate":
#   dial tcp: lookup sidecar-injector-svc.easypj.svc: no such host
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Pod Creation Hangs Then Fails

✗1. kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx → Hangs 10s (default timeout) then FAILS!
✗2. kubectl get svc sidecar-injector-svc -n easypj → NOT FOUND!
✗3. failurePolicy: Fail — blocks ALL pod creation when webhook is down!
✗4. NO pods can be created in the easypj namespace — entire namespace is BRICKED!
3

🔍 Debug — Find the Blocking Webhook

1List all mutating webhooks: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations
→ sidecar-injector exists — but its backend Service is MISSING!
2Check webhook config: kubectl describe mutatingwebhookconfiguration sidecar-injector
→ service: sidecar-injector-svc in namespace easypj — Service DOES NOT EXIST!
3Root cause: The MutatingWebhookConfiguration references a Service that doesn't exist. With failurePolicy: Fail, the API server MUST call the webhook before admitting any pod. Since the webhook is unreachable, ALL pod creations are blocked. Fix: either (A) create the missing Service + webhook server deployment, or (B) delete the webhook configuration to unblock pod creation immediately.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Pod creation hangs 10s → webhook timeout
②
Get webhook config → Service doesn't exist
③
failurePolicy: Fail = blocks ALL requests
④
Delete webhook → unblocks namespace
⑤
Pods created normally!

Tenet: Admission webhooks run BEFORE resource persistence. The default webhook call timeout is 10 seconds if timeoutSeconds isn't explicitly set (this config never set it). If a webhook is unreachable with failurePolicy: Fail, the API server waits out that timeout then MUST reject the request. failurePolicy: Ignore allows requests through when the webhook is down (use for non-critical webhooks). Always ensure webhook backends are HA. Check webhook status with kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx:alpine Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "sidecar.easypj.com": Post "https://sidecar-injector-svc.easypj.svc:443/mutate": dial tcp: lookup sidecar-injector-svc.easypj.svc: no such host
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx:alpine pod/test-pod created ✅ Pod admitted successfully!
5

🔧 Fix — Delete the Broken Webhook

BASH — Remove blocking webhook to restore pod creation
# Immediate fix: DELETE the broken webhook configuration
kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration sidecar-injector

# Now pods can be created again!
kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx:alpine
kubectl get pods -n easypj
6

✅ Verify — Pods Created Successfully

kubectl run test-pod -n easypj --image=nginx succeeds immediately. Key: failurePolicy: Fail blocks ALL requests when webhook is down. Use failurePolicy: Ignore for non-critical webhooks. Always ensure webhook backend is highly available.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
kubectl delete ns easypj
kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration sidecar-injector --ignore-not-found
S79
🧪 SCENARIO S79 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture Validating Webhook

Validating Webhook Rejects ALL Pods — namespaceSelector Matches Everything

The Problem: A validating webhook is configured to reject pods WITHOUT resource limits — but only in the easypj namespace. However, the namespaceSelector is empty {}, which matches ALL namespaces. Now NO pods can be created ANYWHERE in the cluster — even kube-system pods are blocked. Your job: fix the namespaceSelector to target only the easypj namespace, restoring normal pod creation everywhere else.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Validating Webhook with Empty namespaceSelector (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj team deploys a validating webhook to enforce resource limits. The intention: reject pods without limits ONLY in the easypj namespace. But a typo — namespaceSelector: {} (empty, matches everything) — causes the webhook to reject ALL pods cluster-wide. kube-system pods can't restart. CoreDNS gets rejected. The entire cluster grinds to a halt because no pods can be created ANYWHERE.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S79): 
validating-webhook/
├── 01-namespace.yaml                    ← Target namespace: easypj
├── 02-validating-webhook-config.yaml     ← BUG: namespaceSelector: {} (matches ALL!)
├── 03-webhook-config-fixed.yaml          ← FIX: namespaceSelector: {environment: easypj}
└── 04-namespace-label.yaml               ← Label ns: environment=easypj
BASH — Create webhook that matches ALL namespaces
# Create ValidatingWebhookConfiguration with WRONG namespaceSelector
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: require-resource-limits
webhooks:
- name: limits.easypj.com
  clientConfig:
    url: https://httpbin.org/post    # External URL (will reject everything)
  rules:
  - operations: ["CREATE"]
    apiGroups: [""]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    resources: ["pods"]
  failurePolicy: Fail
  sideEffects: None
  admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels: {}      # ❌ BUG! EMPTY = matches ALL namespaces!
EOF

# Try to create pod in DEFAULT namespace — REJECTED!
kubectl run test -n default --image=nginx:alpine
# ❌ Error: admission webhook "limits.easypj.com" denied the request
# This should ONLY apply to the easypj namespace!
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Webhook Rejects Pods in ALL Namespaces

✗1. kubectl run test -n default --image=nginx → REJECTED!
✗2. kubectl get pods -n kube-system → CoreDNS pods can't restart!
✗3. namespaceSelector: {} matches EVERYTHING — should only match easypj!
✗4. Entire cluster is affected — critical system pods BLOCKED!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Is the Webhook Affecting All Namespaces?

1Check webhook config: kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration require-resource-limits -o yaml | grep -A5 namespaceSelector
→ matchLabels: {} — empty selector matches ALL namespaces!
2Root cause: namespaceSelector: {} (empty) matches every namespace in the cluster. To target only specific namespaces, use matchLabels with actual labels like 'matchLabels: {environment: easypj}'. Fix: update the namespaceSelector to specifically target the easypj namespace.
3Check namespace labels: kubectl get ns easypj --show-labels
→ Namespace needs label 'environment: easypj' for the selector to work correctly after fix. Without labels on the target namespace, even a correct selector won't match unless the namespace is labeled.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Pods rejected in ALL namespaces → webhook too broad
②
Check namespaceSelector → {} (empty)
③
Empty selector matches every namespace!
④
Delete webhook → fix selector with labels
⑤
Only easypj namespace affected → cluster healthy!

Tenet: namespaceSelector in admission webhooks determines which namespaces the webhook applies to. Empty {} matches all namespaces (omitting namespaceSelector entirely also matches all). Use matchLabels with actual namespace labels to scope webhooks. For exclusion, use namespaceSelector.matchExpressions with NotIn/DoesNotExist operators.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl run test -n default --image=nginx:alpine Error from server: admission webhook "limits.easypj.com" denied the request: pods in namespace "default" require resource limits
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl run test -n default --image=nginx:alpine pod/test created ✅ Default namespace unaffected! Webhook scoped to easypj only.
5

🔧 Fix — Delete Broken Webhook + Add Label to Namespace

BASH — Fix namespaceSelector and recreate correctly
# Step 1: DELETE the broken webhook (unblocks all namespaces immediately!)
kubectl delete validatingwebhookconfiguration require-resource-limits

# Step 2: Label the target namespace
kubectl create ns easypj 2>/dev/null
kubectl label ns easypj environment=easypj --overwrite

# Step 3: Recreate the webhook with a CORRECT, scoped namespaceSelector
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: require-resource-limits
webhooks:
- name: limits.easypj.com
  clientConfig:
    url: https://httpbin.org/post
  rules:
  - operations: ["CREATE"]
    apiGroups: [""]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    resources: ["pods"]
  failurePolicy: Fail
  sideEffects: None
  admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]
  namespaceSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: easypj   # ✅ Only matches the labeled easypj namespace now!
EOF
6

✅ Verify — Pods Can Be Created in Non-Easypj Namespaces, Webhook Still Scopes to easypj

kubectl run test -n default --image=nginx succeeds, and a resource-limit-less pod in the easypj namespace is still correctly rejected. Key: namespaceSelector: {} matches ALL namespaces — and omitting namespaceSelector entirely behaves the SAME way (also matches all), they are not different. Always use specific matchLabels to scope a webhook to particular namespaces.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH
kubectl delete ns easypj --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete validatingwebhookconfiguration require-resource-limits --ignore-not-found
S80
🧪 SCENARIO S80 — Category 4: Cluster Architecture CNI Comparison

NetworkPolicy Works on Calico but Silently Fails on Flannel — CNI Comparison

The Problem: You apply the same NetworkPolicy across 3 clusters: kind-cl1 (Calico), kind-cl2 (Flannel), and kind-cl3 (Cilium). On cl1 and cl3, the policy blocks traffic correctly. But on cl2 (Flannel), traffic flows through UNRESTRICTED — Flannel does NOT support NetworkPolicy natively. The policy appears to "apply" but does nothing. Your job: verify NetworkPolicy behavior across CNIs, identify that Flannel silently ignores NetworkPolicies, and understand which CNIs support NetworkPolicy enforcement.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 3,4,5 — kind-cl1 (Calico), kind-cl2 (Flannel), kind-cl3 (Cilium)
1

📋 Apply Same NetworkPolicy Across 3 CNI Clusters (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj security team creates a NetworkPolicy to isolate the API namespace. They test on the dev cluster (Calico) — works perfectly. They apply to staging (Flannel) — policy is accepted by kubectl but traffic flows through! A security audit discovers pods in the staging cluster have been communicating unrestricted for 3 months. Flannel accepted the NetworkPolicy YAML but silently ignored it. The staging environment has had ZERO network security.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S80): 
cni-comparison/
├── 01-netpol-test-ns.yaml          ← netpol-test namespace (applied on ALL 3 clusters)
├── 02-web+api-pods.yaml            ← Two pods: web, api (for connectivity test)
├── 03-deny-all-netpol.yaml         ← Default-deny NetworkPolicy (Ingress)
├── 04-cni-matrix.md                ← CNI comparison: Calico/Cilium ✅, Flannel ❌
└── 05-migrate-flannel-to-calico.sh ← Fix: replace Flannel with Calico
BASH — Test NetworkPolicy across different CNI plugins
# On EACH cluster (cl1/Calico, cl2/Flannel, cl3/Cilium):
# 1. Create test namespace and pods
kubectl create ns netpol-test
kubectl run web -n netpol-test --image=nginx:alpine --labels=app=web
kubectl run api -n netpol-test --image=nginx:alpine --labels=app=api
kubectl expose pod api -n netpol-test --port=80

# 2. Test connectivity BEFORE policy (should work everywhere)
kubectl exec web -n netpol-test -- wget -O- --timeout=3 api.netpol-test.svc
# ✅ All 3 clusters: connection succeeds

# 3. Apply default-deny NetworkPolicy
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all
  namespace: netpol-test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
EOF

# 4. Test AFTER policy:
kubectl exec web -n netpol-test -- wget -O- --timeout=3 api.netpol-test.svc
# cl1 (Calico): ❌ TIMEOUT — Policy WORKS! ✅
# cl2 (Flannel): ✅ SUCCESS — Policy IGNORED! ❌ BUG!
# cl3 (Cilium): ❌ TIMEOUT — Policy WORKS! ✅
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Flannel Silently Ignores NetworkPolicy

✗1. NetworkPolicy applied on cl2 (Flannel) — kubectl shows it EXISTS!
✗2. Traffic still flows unrestricted — policy has NO EFFECT!
✗3. Same policy works on cl1 (Calico) and cl3 (Cilium) — blocks traffic!
✗4. Flannel doesn't support NetworkPolicy — but Kubernetes doesn't warn you!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Does the Policy Only Work on Some Clusters?

1Check CNI on each cluster: kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep -E "calico|flannel|cilium"
→ cl1: calico-node, cl2: flannel, cl3: cilium
2Understand CNI NetworkPolicy support: Calico (✅), Cilium (✅), Weave (✅) support NetworkPolicy. Flannel (❌) does NOT support NetworkPolicy natively. Canal = Flannel networking + Calico policy (provides NetworkPolicy on top of Flannel).
→ Flannel only provides pod networking — ZERO policy enforcement!
3Root cause: Flannel is a simple overlay network (VXLAN/host-gw) that only handles pod-to-pod connectivity. It does NOT implement NetworkPolicy enforcement. Kubernetes accepts the NetworkPolicy YAML and stores it in etcd, but without a CNI that implements policy enforcement, the rules are never applied to iptables/eBPF. Fix: use Calico, Cilium, or Canal (Flannel+Calico policy) for environments requiring NetworkPolicy.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Policy works on Calico/Cilium → Flannel fails
②
Same YAML → different behavior = CNI issue
③
Flannel: no NetworkPolicy support at all
④
Kubernetes doesn't warn — policy stored, ignored
⑤
Replace Flannel with Calico/Cilium!

Tenet: NetworkPolicy resources are just YAML — enforcement depends on the CNI plugin. Calico, Cilium, Weave implement NetworkPolicy natively. Flannel does NOT (only provides pod networking). Canal = Flannel networking + Calico policy controller. Always verify NetworkPolicy enforcement by testing actual traffic, not just kubectl apply.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl exec web -n netpol-test -- wget -O- --timeout=3 api.netpol-test.svc <!DOCTYPE html> <html> ... <h1>Welcome to nginx!</h1> ❌ Connection SUCCEEDS — Policy IGNORED on Flannel!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl exec web -n netpol-test -- wget -O- --timeout=3 api.netpol-test.svc wget: download timed out ✅ Policy ENFORCES — traffic blocked as expected!
5

🔧 Fix — Replace Flannel with Calico on cl2

BASH — Migrate from Flannel to Calico for NetworkPolicy support
# On cl2 (Flannel): Delete Flannel, install Calico
kubectl delete -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flannel-io/flannel/master/Documentation/kube-flannel.yml --ignore-not-found
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectcalico/calico/v3.28.0/manifests/calico.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l k8s-app=calico-node -n kube-system --timeout=120s
# Re-test the NetworkPolicy — now it WORKS!
6

✅ Verify — NetworkPolicy Enforced on All 3 Clusters

Now all clusters enforce the policy. Key CNI comparison: Calico = BGP routing + NetworkPolicy ✅. Flannel = VXLAN only, no NetworkPolicy ❌. Cilium = eBPF + L3/L4/L7 NetworkPolicy ✅. Always verify your CNI supports NetworkPolicy before relying on it.

7

🧹 Cleanup — On All 3 Clusters

BASH — Run on each cluster
kubectl delete ns netpol-test

🌐 Category 5: Services & Networking Lab ScenariosS81-S100

🟢 Service Types, DNS, Network Policies, Ingress & TLS

These 20 scenarios cover the full networking stack: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, Headless Services, CoreDNS troubleshooting, NetworkPolicy enforcement, Ingress routing, TLS certificates, and cert-manager. Each scenario deploys part of the easypj/jobpost application with intentional networking bugs.

📌 S81–S85: Service Types Deep Dive

S81
🧪 SCENARIO S81 — Category 5: Services & Networking ClusterIP Debug

ClusterIP Service Shows <none> Endpoints — Selector Doesn't Match Pod Labels

The Problem: You deploy the easypj-web Deployment with 3 replicas. Pods are Running. You create a ClusterIP Service to expose them, but kubectl get endpoints shows <none>. No traffic reaches the pods. The Service selector says app: easypj-web but the pod labels say tier: web — a label mismatch. Your job: find the selector mismatch, fix the Service to match pod labels, and verify traffic flows.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — CKA exam practice cluster
1

📋 Deploy easypj-web Pods + Broken ClusterIP Service (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj job board's web frontend is deployed — 3 pods running Nginx. The DevOps lead creates a ClusterIP Service to expose them internally. kubectl get svc shows the Service exists with a ClusterIP. But kubectl get endpoints shows <none>. The job board homepage returns "connection refused." 500 employers trying to post jobs see a blank page. The Service selector says app: easypj-web, but the pods were labeled tier: web by mistake. The label mismatch means zero traffic routes to any pod.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S81): 
clusterip-debug/
├── 01-namespace.yaml              ← kubectl create ns easypj-net
├── 02-web-deployment.yaml         ← Deployment with labels {tier: web} (correct for pods)
├── 03-broken-service.yaml         ← Service with BUG: selector {app: easypj-web} (WRONG!)
├── 04-fixed-service.yaml          ← Service FIX: selector {tier: web} (matches pods!)
└── 05-verify-connectivity.sh      ← curl from test pod → Service → pods
BASH — Deploy pods with labels {tier: web}, create Service with WRONG selector 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S81: ClusterIP Service — Selector Mismatch
# ============================================

# STEP 1: Create namespace and deploy web pods
kubectl create namespace easypj-net
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: easypj-web
  namespace: easypj-net
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      tier: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        tier: web         # Pods have label {tier: web}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
EOF
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l tier=web -n easypj-net --timeout=60s

# STEP 2: Create Service with WRONG selector (THE BUG!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: easypj-web-svc
  namespace: easypj-net
spec:
  selector:
    app: easypj-web    # ❌ BUG! Pods have {tier: web}, NOT {app: easypj-web}!
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
  type: ClusterIP
EOF

# STEP 3: Check endpoints — EMPTY!
kubectl get endpoints easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net
# ❌ NAME             ENDPOINTS   AGE
#    easypj-web-svc   <none>      5s   ← NO ENDPOINTS! SELECTOR MISMATCH!

# The APP STORY:
# "The website is down! 500 employers can't post jobs!"
# Pods are Running 1/1 — all 3 healthy. Service exists with ClusterIP.
# But endpoints show <none>. The selector doesn't match ANY pod.
# Traffic goes to the Service IP and DIES — zero pods receive it.
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Endpoints Empty, No Traffic Routed

✗1. kubectl get endpoints easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net → ENDPOINTS: <none>
✗2. kubectl get pods -n easypj-net → 3 pods Running 1/1 — pods are FINE!
✗3. kubectl get svc easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net → ClusterIP EXISTS but useless!
✗4. Any request to the Service IP returns connection refused — website is DOWN!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Are Endpoints Empty When Pods Are Running?

1Check Service selector: kubectl get svc easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net -o yaml | grep -A3 selector
→ selector: app: easypj-web — looking for pods with label {app: easypj-web}
2Check pod labels: kubectl get pods -n easypj-net --show-labels
→ Pods have labels {tier: web, app: easypj-web-NOT-PRESENT} — label MISMATCH!
3Compare selector vs labels: Service wants {app: easypj-web}. Pods have {tier: web}. These are DIFFERENT labels — the Service selector is looking for a label that doesn't exist on any pod!
4Root cause: The Service selector {app: easypj-web} does not match any pod labels. Pods are labeled {tier: web}. The Service's EndpointSlice controller watches pods matching the selector — since no pods match, endpoints stay empty. Fix: change the Service selector to {tier: web} to match the actual pod labels, OR add label {app: easypj-web} to the pod template.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Endpoints <none> → selector issue
②
Check Service selector → {app: easypj-web}
③
Check pod labels → {tier: web} — MISMATCH!
④
Fix selector to {tier: web}
⑤
Endpoints populated → traffic flows!

Tenet: Service selectors are the glue between Services and Pods. If the selector doesn't match ANY pod's labels, endpoints stay empty forever. The #1 cause of "Service not working" is a selector/label mismatch. Always verify: (1) kubectl get endpoints → must show pod IPs, (2) kubectl get pods --show-labels → compare with Service selector. On CKA: this is the most common Service debugging task — find and fix the selector mismatch.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl get endpoints easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net NAME ENDPOINTS AGE easypj-web-svc <none> 2m ← SELECTOR MISMATCH — NO PODS MATCHED!
$ kubectl get pods -n easypj-net --show-labels NAME READY STATUS LABELS easypj-web-7d8f9-abc 1/1 Running tier=web,pod-template-hash=7d8f9 easypj-web-7d8f9-def 1/1 Running tier=web,pod-template-hash=7d8f9 easypj-web-7d8f9-ghi 1/1 Running tier=web,pod-template-hash=7d8f9
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl get endpoints easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net NAME ENDPOINTS AGE easypj-web-svc 10.244.1.5:80,10.244.2.3:80,10.244.1.6:80 3m ← ENDPOINTS POPULATED!
$ kubectl run test --rm -it --image=busybox -n easypj-net -- wget -qO- --timeout=3 easypj-web-svc <!DOCTYPE html><html>...<h1>Welcome to nginx!</h1> ← TRAFFIC FLOWS!
5

🔧 Fix — Patch Service Selector to Match Pod Labels

BASH — Fix the selector mismatch 
# Option 1: Patch the Service selector (CKA fast method)
kubectl patch svc easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/selector/app"},{"op":"add","path":"/spec/selector/tier","value":"web"}]'

# Option 2: Delete and recreate with correct selector
kubectl delete svc easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net
kubectl expose deployment easypj-web -n easypj-net --name=easypj-web-svc --port=80 --target-port=80

# Verify endpoints populated
kubectl get endpoints easypj-web-svc -n easypj-net
6

✅ Verify — Endpoints Populated, Traffic Flows to Pods

kubectl get endpoints shows 3 pod IPs. wget from a test pod returns the Nginx welcome page. Key: Service selector MUST match pod labels exactly. Labels are key-value pairs — both key AND value must match. Use kubectl get pods --show-labels to verify before creating Services.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH — copy & paste to clean up 
kubectl delete namespace easypj-net
S82
🧪 SCENARIO S82 — Category 5: Services & Networking NodePort Policy

NodePort 30080 Returns Empty Response — externalTrafficPolicy: Local Drops Cross-Node Traffic

The Problem: You expose easypj-web via NodePort 30080 on a 2-node kind cluster (cp + wk1). External requests work when hitting the node WITH the pod, but return empty response / timeout when hitting the node WITHOUT a pod. The Service has externalTrafficPolicy: Local which routes traffic ONLY to pods on the SAME node — cross-node traffic is DROPPED. Your job: identify the policy issue, switch to externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster, and verify traffic routes to pods on ALL nodes.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
1

📋 Deploy Single Pod + NodePort with externalTrafficPolicy: Local (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj ops team exposes the web frontend via NodePort 30080 so the load balancer can reach it. Half the external requests work, half fail. The Service uses externalTrafficPolicy: Local — kube-proxy only forwards traffic to pods on the SAME node. When the external LB hits node wk1 (no web pod), the connection hangs and times out. 50% of users see a blank page. The marketing campaign just launched — every failed request is a lost employer.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S82): 
nodeport-policy/
├── 01-web-pod.yaml                ← Bare Pod (runs on cp OR wk1)
├── 02-broken-nodeport-svc.yaml    ← NodePort 30080 with BUG: externalTrafficPolicy: Local
├── 03-test-cross-node.sh          ← curl to both nodes → one fails!
└── 04-fixed-cluster-policy.yaml   ← FIX: externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
BASH — Deploy web pod + NodePort with externalTrafficPolicy: Local 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S82: NodePort — externalTrafficPolicy: Local
# ============================================

# STEP 1: Create namespace and deploy a single web pod
kubectl create ns easypj-web
kubectl run web-pod -n easypj-web --image=nginx:alpine --labels=app=web --port=80
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/web-pod -n easypj-web --timeout=60s

# STEP 2: Find which node the pod runs on
kubectl get pod web-pod -n easypj-web -o wide
# NAME      READY   STATUS    NODE
# web-pod   1/1     Running   cp   ← Pod is on cp node

# STEP 3: Create NodePort with externalTrafficPolicy: Local (THE BUG!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport
  namespace: easypj-web
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    nodePort: 30080
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local   # ❌ BUG! Only routes to pods on the RECEIVING node!
EOF

# STEP 4: Test from cp node (where pod IS) — WORKS!
NODE_CP=$(kubectl get node cp -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[0].address}')
curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://$NODE_CP:30080 | head -3
# ✅ Welcome to nginx! (pod is on this node)

# STEP 5: Test from wk1 node (where pod IS NOT) — FAILS!
NODE_WK1=$(kubectl get node wk1 -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[0].address}')
curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://$NODE_WK1:30080
# ❌ curl: (52) Empty reply from server — CROSS-NODE TRAFFIC DROPPED!

# The APP STORY:
# 50% of users can't reach the job board!
# The external load balancer round-robins between cp:30080 and wk1:30080.
# cp works (pod is there), wk1 fails (no pod, Local policy drops traffic).
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Half the NodePort Requests Fail

✗1. curl http://CP-IP:30080 → Welcome to nginx! (pod on cp → WORKS)
✗2. curl http://WK1-IP:30080 → Empty reply / Timeout (no pod on wk1 → FAILS)
✗3. kubectl get svc web-nodeport -n easypj-web -o yaml | grep externalTrafficPolicy → Local
✗4. 50% traffic loss — externalTrafficPolicy: Local drops cross-node requests!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Does Traffic Fail on wk1 But Not cp?

1Check pod location: kubectl get pod web-pod -n easypj-web -o wide
→ Pod runs on cp — only 1 of 2 nodes has the pod!
2Check traffic policy: kubectl get svc web-nodeport -n easypj-web -o yaml | grep externalTrafficPolicy
→ externalTrafficPolicy: Local — traffic only forwarded to pods on RECEIVING node!
3Understand Local vs Cluster: Local preserves source IP but doesn't forward to other nodes. If the receiving node has no matching pod → traffic DROPPED. Cluster (default) forwards via kube-proxy SNAT to any node with a matching pod → traffic WORKS but source IP is lost.
4Root cause: externalTrafficPolicy: Local restricts traffic to pods on the SAME node. With only 1 pod on cp, requests to wk1:30080 find no local pod and are dropped. Fix: change to externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster for cross-node routing, OR scale pods to run on every node if source IP preservation is needed.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
NodePort 30080 → half fail
②
Check policy → Local
③
Pod only on cp → wk1 drops
④
Change to Cluster policy
⑤
Both nodes serve traffic!

Tenet: externalTrafficPolicy controls NodePort/LoadBalancer routing. Local = source IP preserved, traffic stays on receiving node (drops if no local pod). Cluster (default) = traffic forwarded to any node via SNAT, source IP lost. For CKA: understand the trade-off — Local for source IP, Cluster for availability. This is a common exam scenario: "why does NodePort work from one node but not another?"

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://WK1-IP:30080 curl: (52) Empty reply from server ← DROPPED! Pod is on cp, not wk1!
$ kubectl get svc web-nodeport -n easypj-web -o yaml | grep externalTrafficPolicy externalTrafficPolicy: Local ← ROOT CAUSE!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://WK1-IP:30080 | head -3 <!DOCTYPE html>...Welcome to nginx! ← ROUTED TO POD ON cp VIA CLUSTER!
$ curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://CP-IP:30080 | head -3 <!DOCTYPE html>...Welcome to nginx! ← BOTH NODES NOW WORK!
5

🔧 Fix — Switch to Cluster Traffic Policy

BASH — Fix externalTrafficPolicy 
# Option 1: Patch the Service (CKA fast method)
kubectl patch svc web-nodeport -n easypj-web --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/externalTrafficPolicy","value":"Cluster"}]'

# Option 2: Scale deployment so pods run on ALL nodes (if Local is required)
kubectl create deployment web-multi -n easypj-web --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2
kubectl expose deployment web-multi -n easypj-web --type=NodePort --port=80 --target-port=80 --name=web-np-cluster

# Verify both nodes now respond
curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://$NODE_CP:30080 | head -1
curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://$NODE_WK1:30080 | head -1

✅ Verify — Both Nodes Serve Traffic Successfully

Both node IPs now return the Nginx welcome page. Key: externalTrafficPolicy: Local drops cross-node traffic if the receiving node has no local pod. Use Cluster for availability when source IP preservation is not critical. For CKA: this is tested — know to check externalTrafficPolicy when NodePort works inconsistently across nodes.

LoadBalancer Service Stuck Pending Forever — No Cloud Load Balancer Controller

The Problem: You create a LoadBalancer Service for easypj-web to expose it externally. But the Service stays in Pending state forever — EXTERNAL-IP shows <pending>. On bare-metal/kind clusters, there is NO cloud-controller-manager to provision an actual load balancer. Kubernetes creates the Service but nothing fulfills it. Your job: identify why LoadBalancer won't work on kind, and implement a workaround using NodePort + port-forward or install MetalLB to simulate a load balancer IP.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — CKA exam practice cluster
1

📋 Create LoadBalancer Service on Bare-Metal Kind — Stays Pending (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj team deploys their web frontend on a self-managed kind cluster. Management wants external access without port-forwarding. The DevOps lead creates a type: LoadBalancer Service, expecting an external IP. Minutes pass. Hours pass. EXTERNAL-IP stays <pending> FOREVER. No cloud controller exists on bare metal to provision a load balancer. The CTO wants to demo the app to investors in 30 minutes. Without external access, the demo is dead.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S83): 
loadbalancer-pending/
├── 01-namespace.yaml             ← kubectl create ns easypj-lb
├── 02-web-deployment.yaml        ← Simple nginx deployment (3 replicas)
├── 03-lb-service-pending.yaml    ← BUG: type: LoadBalancer → EXTERNAL-IP: <pending> FOREVER!
├── 04-metallb-install.yaml       ← MetalLB installation (THE FIX for bare metal)
└── 05-lb-service-fixed.yaml      ← LoadBalancer with MetalLB → gets IP!
BASH — Create LoadBalancer Service, watch it stay Pending forever 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S83: LoadBalancer Stuck Pending — No Cloud Controller
# ============================================

# STEP 1: Create namespace and deploy web pods
kubectl create namespace easypj-lb
kubectl create deployment easypj-web -n easypj-lb --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3
kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/easypj-web -n easypj-lb --timeout=60s

# STEP 2: Create LoadBalancer Service (THE BUG!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-lb
  namespace: easypj-lb
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer    # ❌ BUG! No cloud controller on bare metal!
  selector:
    app: easypj-web
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
EOF

# STEP 3: Check the Service — STUCK PENDING!
kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb
# ❌ BUG! Output:
# NAME      TYPE           CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)        AGE
# web-lb    LoadBalancer   10.96.45.67    <pending>     80:30001/TCP   5m

# STEP 4: Describe the Service — no events, nothing happening
kubectl describe svc web-lb -n easypj-lb
# ❌ No events. No errors. Just... nothing. EXTERNAL-IP stays pending forever.

# The APP STORY:
# "Why is the LoadBalancer still pending? It's been 2 hours!"
# On AWS/GCP/Azure: cloud-controller-manager auto-creates an actual LB.
# On bare metal/kind/minikube: NO cloud controller exists.
# The Service is valid but no controller fulfills the LoadBalancer request.
# The investor demo is in 30 minutes. External access is BLOCKED.
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — EXTERNAL-IP Stays <pending> Forever

✗1. kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb → EXTERNAL-IP: <pending>
✗2. kubectl describe svc web-lb -n easypj-lb → NO events — nothing is happening!
✗3. NodePort IS allocated (30001) — traffic works via NodePort, but EXTERNAL-IP never assigned!
✗4. No cloud-controller-manager pod in kube-system — bare metal has no LB provisioner!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Is LoadBalancer Stuck Pending?

1Check if cloud controller exists: kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep cloud-controller
→ NO RESULTS! No cloud-controller-manager on bare metal/kind!
2Check Service events: kubectl describe svc web-lb -n easypj-lb | grep -A10 Events
→ No events at all — the Service is waiting for a controller that doesn't exist!
3Understand LoadBalancer in different environments: AWS EKS → creates AWS NLB/ALB. GCP GKE → creates Google Cloud LB. Azure AKS → creates Azure LB. Bare Metal / Kind / Minikube → NOTHING creates the LB. On bare metal, you need MetalLB (Layer 2 or BGP mode) to simulate a LoadBalancer by assigning IPs from a pool.
4Root cause: Kubernetes LoadBalancer Service type requires a cloud-controller-manager or an external load balancer provider (like MetalLB) to provision an external IP. On kind (bare metal), no such controller exists. Fix: install MetalLB to provide LoadBalancer IPs, OR use NodePort + port-forward as a quick workaround, OR switch to a cloud-managed cluster.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
EXTERNAL-IP <pending> → check cloud controller
②
No cloud-controller-manager pod!
③
Bare metal needs MetalLB or similar
④
Install MetalLB → assign IP pool
⑤
LoadBalancer gets IP → external access!

Tenet: LoadBalancer Services require a controller that provisions an actual load balancer. On cloud platforms, cloud-controller-manager does this automatically. On bare metal, you need MetalLB (or similar). Without a controller, LoadBalancer stays Pending forever. On CKA: you'll be tested on understanding why LoadBalancer doesn't work on non-cloud clusters and the alternatives (NodePort, port-forward, Ingress with NodePort).

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE web-lb LoadBalancer 10.96.45.67 <pending> 80:30001/TCP 10m ← FOREVER PENDING!
$ kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep cloud-controller (no results) ← NO CLOUD CONTROLLER EXISTS ON BARE METAL!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix (with MetalLB)
$ kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE web-lb LoadBalancer 10.96.45.67 172.18.255.200 80:30001/TCP 12m ← IP ASSIGNED!
$ curl -s http://172.18.255.200 | head -3 <!DOCTYPE html>...Welcome to nginx! ← EXTERNAL ACCESS WORKS!
5

🔧 Fix — Install MetalLB for Bare-Metal LoadBalancer

BASH — Install MetalLB + configure IP pool 
# Option 1 (QUICK FIX): Use NodePort already assigned + port-forward
kubectl port-forward svc/web-lb 8080:80 -n easypj-lb &
curl localhost:8080

# Option 2 (PROPER FIX): Install MetalLB for real LoadBalancer IPs
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metallb/metallb/v0.14.5/config/manifests/metallb-native.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods -l app=metallb -n metallb-system --timeout=120s

# Configure IP address pool — derive the range from kind's ACTUAL docker subnet
# (kind subnets look like 172.18.0.0/16, not 0.0.0.0/16 — extract the real first two octets)
SUBNET=$(docker network inspect kind -f '{{range .IPAM.Config}}{{.Subnet}}{{end}}' 2>/dev/null | head -1)
BASE=$(echo "$SUBNET" | cut -d. -f1-2)
POOL_RANGE="${BASE}.255.200-${BASE}.255.250"
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1
kind: IPAddressPool
metadata:
  name: my-pool
  namespace: metallb-system
spec:
  addresses:
  - ${POOL_RANGE}
---
# L2Advertisement — announces the pool's IPs over L2/ARP so nodes can route to them
apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1
kind: L2Advertisement
metadata:
  name: my-l2-adv
  namespace: metallb-system
EOF

# Now check the Service — EXTERNAL-IP assigned!
kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb
6

✅ Verify — LoadBalancer Has External IP, Traffic Flows

kubectl get svc web-lb -n easypj-lb shows EXTERNAL-IP assigned by MetalLB. curl to the external IP returns the Nginx page. Key: LoadBalancer requires a controller. Cloud → cloud-controller-manager. Bare metal → MetalLB. For CKA: know that LoadBalancer won't work out-of-the-box on non-cloud clusters.

kubectl delete namespace metallb-system --ignore-not-found 2>/dev/null
S84
🧪 SCENARIO S84 — Category 5: Services & Networking Headless Service

StatefulSet Pods Can't Resolve Each Other — Headless Service Missing clusterIP: None

The Problem: The easypj-db StatefulSet needs stable per-pod DNS: easypj-db-0.easypj-db-svc should resolve to pod-0's IP, easypj-db-1 to pod-1's IP. But nslookup easypj-db-0.easypj-db-svc returns the Service's ClusterIP instead of the individual pod IP. The headless Service was created WITHOUT clusterIP: None — so it's just a regular ClusterIP Service. Pod-specific DNS doesn't work. Your job: identify the missing clusterIP: None, fix the Service to be truly headless, and verify per-pod DNS resolution.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — CKA exam practice cluster
1

📋 Create StatefulSet with "Headless" Service — But clusterIP: None Is Missing (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: The easypj database team deploys PostgreSQL as a StatefulSet with 3 replicas. Replication requires each pod to know its peers' IPs for streaming replication. They create a Service named "easypj-db-svc" thinking it's headless. But PostgreSQL replication fails — pods can't discover each other by DNS name. Each pod tries nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc but gets the Service's ClusterIP instead of pod-1's actual IP. The database cluster can't form. 50,000 job listings are at risk because the DB is running in single-instance mode with no replication.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for easypj/jobpost (S84): 
headless-service/
├── 01-namespace.yaml             ← kubectl create ns easypj-db
├── 02-broken-headless-svc.yaml   ← Service MISSING clusterIP: None (THE BUG!)
├── 03-statefulset.yaml           ← StatefulSet with serviceName: easypj-db-svc
├── 04-fixed-headless-svc.yaml    ← Service WITH clusterIP: None (HEADLESS!)
└── 05-dns-verify.sh              ← nslookup per-pod DNS records
BASH — Deploy StatefulSet with broken "headless" Service 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S84: Headless Service Missing clusterIP: None
# ============================================

# STEP 1: Create namespace
kubectl create namespace easypj-db

# STEP 2: Create Service WITHOUT clusterIP: None (THE BUG!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: easypj-db-svc
  namespace: easypj-db
spec:
  # ❌ BUG! Missing: clusterIP: None — this is NOT headless!
  selector:
    app: easypj-db
  ports:
  - port: 5432
    targetPort: 5432
EOF

# STEP 3: Create StatefulSet pointing to this Service
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: easypj-db
  namespace: easypj-db
spec:
  serviceName: easypj-db-svc  # References the broken Service
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: easypj-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: easypj-db
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: nginx:alpine
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db --timeout=60s
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/easypj-db-1 -n easypj-db --timeout=60s

# STEP 4: Test per-pod DNS — CAN'T RESOLVE AT ALL (not "resolves to ClusterIP")!
kubectl exec easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db -- nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc
# ❌ BUG! NXDOMAIN — per-pod DNS records (pod-name.service-name...) are ONLY created for
# HEADLESS Services. A regular ClusterIP Service has no per-pod subdomain entries at all —
# querying "easypj-db-svc" alone would return the ClusterIP, but "easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc" doesn't exist as a name.

# The APP STORY:
# "PostgreSQL replication won't start — peers unreachable!"
# Each pod tries to resolve its peer's per-pod DNS name — and gets NXDOMAIN.
# Replication needs direct pod-to-pod communication via stable per-pod names.
# Those names simply don't exist without a headless Service.
# Without clusterIP: None, this is just a regular Service with no per-pod DNS at all.
2

⚠️ Observe the Error — Per-Pod DNS Name Doesn't Resolve At All

✗1. nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc → NXDOMAIN — the name doesn't exist (not "resolves to the wrong IP")
✗2. kubectl get svc easypj-db-svc -n easypj-db → CLUSTER-IP shows an IP (not None!)
✗3. Service was created without clusterIP: None — it's just a regular ClusterIP Service!
✗4. PostgreSQL streaming replication FAILS — pods can't discover peer IPs for replication!
3

🔍 Debug — Why Doesn't Headless DNS Work?

1Check Service spec: kubectl get svc easypj-db-svc -n easypj-db -o yaml | grep clusterIP
→ clusterIP: 10.96.45.78 — this is a REGULAR Service, NOT headless!
2Check what headless means: A headless Service (clusterIP: None) does NOT get a ClusterIP. Per-pod DNS A/AAAA records (pod-N.serviceName.namespace.svc.cluster.local resolving directly to pod-N's IP) are ONLY created for a headless Service's selected pods — a regular ClusterIP Service has no per-pod DNS entries at all, so querying one returns NXDOMAIN, not a fallback to the ClusterIP.
3Root cause: The Service spec is missing 'clusterIP: None'. Without this field, Kubernetes assigns a ClusterIP and no per-pod DNS records are ever created — querying a per-pod name returns NXDOMAIN. Fix: delete the Service and recreate it with 'clusterIP: None' in the spec. NOTE: clusterIP is immutable — you CANNOT patch it; you must delete and recreate the Service.
4

🧠 Answer — Diagnostic Tenet & Expected Outputs

🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
nslookup fails NXDOMAIN → not headless
②
Check Service → clusterIP is set!
③
Missing clusterIP: None — key field
④
Delete + recreate with clusterIP: None
⑤
Per-pod DNS resolves → replication works!

Tenet: clusterIP: None is the ONLY field that makes a Service headless. Without it, per-pod DNS records are never created for that Service's pods — a per-pod name lookup fails with NXDOMAIN, it does NOT silently fall back to the ClusterIP. A headless Service is required for StatefulSet pod identity and peer discovery. clusterIP is IMMUTABLE — you cannot patch it. Must delete and recreate. On CKA: this is a common exam trap — "fix the headless Service" actually means delete and recreate with clusterIP: None.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl get svc easypj-db-svc -n easypj-db NAME TYPE CLUSTER-IP EXTERNAL-IP PORT(S) AGE easypj-db-svc ClusterIP 10.96.45.78 <none> 5432/TCP 5m ← HAS ClusterIP!
$ kubectl exec easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db -- nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc Server: 10.96.0.10 ** server can't find easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc.easypj-db.svc.cluster.local: NXDOMAIN ← NO per-pod DNS record exists!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl exec easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db -- nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc Name: easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc.easypj-db.svc.cluster.local Address: 10.244.2.5 ← POD IP! HEADLESS SERVICE WORKS!
5

🔧 Fix — Delete + Recreate Headless Service

BASH — clusterIP is immutable, must delete and recreate 
# Step 1: Delete the broken Service
kubectl delete svc easypj-db-svc -n easypj-db

# Step 2: Recreate with clusterIP: None (HEADLESS!)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: easypj-db-svc
  namespace: easypj-db
spec:
  clusterIP: None  # ← THIS makes it headless!
  selector:
    app: easypj-db
  ports:
  - port: 5432
    targetPort: 5432
EOF

# Step 3: Verify per-pod DNS works
kubectl exec easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db -- nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc
kubectl exec easypj-db-0 -n easypj-db -- nslookup easypj-db-0.easypj-db-svc
6

✅ Verify — Headless Service Returns Individual Pod IPs

nslookup easypj-db-1.easypj-db-svc returns pod-1's actual IP (10.244.x.x), not a ClusterIP. Key: clusterIP: None is the defining characteristic of a headless Service. clusterIP is IMMUTABLE — you cannot patch it. For StatefulSets, headless Services enable stable per-pod DNS for peer discovery.

7

🧹 Cleanup

BASH — copy & paste to clean up 
kubectl delete namespace easypj-db
